[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

The application scaffold is one of the five mandatory components of a Golden Path bundle, but no specification exists for what a scaffold template must contain. Platform Engineering authors scaffolds ad hoc, producing templates that may not satisfy the structural conformance checks in the path's Verification Contract (SC-001, SC-002, SC-003), omit mandatory runtime control stubs that development teams are then expected to wire in themselves, and fail to pre-populate the AI context files that downstream autonomous generation pipelines depend on. A scaffold that does not produce a conformant, pre-wired starting project forces teams to perform structural and compliance setup work that the Golden Path is supposed to eliminate.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

This pattern defines the mandatory structure, required files, parameterization format, and pre-wired control stubs that every Golden Path scaffold template must deliver. A scaffold template stored at `catalog/templates/{path-id}/` is a parameterizable project template that, when instantiated with a small set of required inputs (`service_name`, `team`, `domain`), produces a project that passes all Layer 1 structural conformance checks, includes pre-wired stubs for every mandatory runtime control declared in the path's `constraints.md`, and contains a pre-populated `.ai/` context directory aligned with the path's compliance scope.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Authoring a new Golden Path scaffold template for any workload class
- Auditing an existing scaffold template against the pattern prior to ARB submission
- Remediating scaffold templates that produce services with systematic Layer 1 conformance failures
- Extending an existing scaffold template when a Golden Path version update introduces new structural rules
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Services instantiated from a conforming scaffold pass Layer 1 checks on first pipeline run without team remediation
- Mandatory runtime control stubs (PHI redaction, External Secrets Operator, audit event publisher) are present and correctly wired from the starting commit, not added during code review
- Pre-populated `.ai/` context ensures AI agents operating in the new repository immediately reference the correct Golden Path constraints, eliminating the cold-start context problem
page_texts.8:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#target-audience]

## Target Audience

This pattern is intended for:

- **Platform Engineer**: Authoring Golden Path scaffold templates that satisfy structural conformance checks and include pre-wired runtime control stubs
- **Application Developer**: Consuming scaffold templates to instantiate new services with correct structure and compliance controls from the first commit
- **Enterprise Architect**: Reviewing scaffold templates for ARB submission and verifying alignment with the Golden Path catalog specification
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

The [Enterprise Golden Path Strategy](../../../../strategy/white-papers/engineering/enterprise-golden-path-strategy.md) defines a Golden Path as an end-to-end, parameterizable, executable template that produces a running system when given a small number of application-specific inputs. The application scaffold is the component of that bundle that delivers the starting project structure. The strategy expressly states the scaffold implements "Gainwell's standard structure, dependency management, logging, observability instrumentation, and health check patterns."

Without a specification for what those structures, dependencies, and patterns are, each scaffold reflects the judgment of the engineer who authored it. When a development team instantiates that scaffold and runs their first pipeline, conformance gate failures become the first discovery mechanism for scaffold gaps — after the team has already committed to the project structure. Scaffold defects impose remediation cost on every team that consumes the path.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Scaffold templates are stored in the Golden Path Catalog at `catalog/templates/{path-id}/`. Each template is a directory of Nunjucks-parameterized files accompanied by a `template.yaml` manifest (Backstage Software Template format) that declares the required inputs, optional parameters with defaults, and path constants. Project template files live under a `skeleton/` subdirectory. Filename tokens use `__variable__` substitution (e.g., the project root directory is named `__service_name__/`), and file content uses `${{ values.variable }}` Nunjucks expressions — the same delimiter Backstage's `fetch:template` action uses. The scaffold runner (`node scaffold.js`) processes the inputs and produces a populated project directory. When a developer portal platform is adopted, `node scaffold.js` is replaced by the platform's `fetch:template` action with no changes to template files.

Layer 1 conformance checks are implemented by the Conformance Gate (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001), which runs `conformance-check --path-id {path-id} --check structural` as a CI/CD pipeline step. The Verification Contract (PTN-GOV-AI-003) defines the exact rules that `conformance-check` evaluates. For GP-001 (HIPAA REST Microservice), the structural checks include SC-001 (directory structure), SC-002 (OpenAPI spec presence), and SC-003 (health endpoint in OpenAPI spec). If the scaffold does not produce a project satisfying these checks from the first commit, teams encounter conformance gate failures before writing a single line of business logic.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

The absence of a scaffold specification creates several observable failure modes:

- **Structural failures on first run**: Scaffold produces a project without `src/api/`, `src/domain/`, `src/infrastructure/` subdirectories, immediately failing SC-001. Teams add the directories, but the scaffold has not enforced the layer separation the directory structure is meant to signal.
- **Missing OpenAPI spec**: Scaffold produces no `docs/openapi.yaml`, failing SC-002 and SC-003. Teams author the spec from scratch with no template, producing inconsistent API contract definitions.
- **Absent control stubs**: Scaffold produces a plain Spring Boot or FastAPI starter without `PiiRedactionSerializer` integration, External Secrets Operator configuration, or `AuditEventPublisher` wiring. Teams add these later, but the timing means they are often added during code review rather than during initial development — after violations may already be in the working branch.
- **Cold-start AI context**: Scaffold produces no `.ai/` directory. AI agents operating in the repository default to training data rather than the Golden Path catalog, generating novel architecture instead of catalog-conforming implementations.
page_texts.13:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- Scaffold must produce a compilable, runnable project with no manual post-instantiation steps; teams should not need to resolve compile errors or missing imports before they can run the health endpoint
- Control stubs must be correct stubs — the right imports, the right framework hooks, the right configuration references — not placeholder comments instructing teams to add controls later
- Scaffold must be language/framework-specific; a single framework-agnostic scaffold template cannot satisfy language-specific structural requirements; each workload class requires at least one scaffold per approved stack
- Parameterization scope is intentionally narrow: `service_name`, `team`, `domain` are the only required inputs; anything beyond that is a configuration decision that belongs in `service.yaml` and `context.yaml`, not the instantiation prompt
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

A conforming Golden Path scaffold template is a Nunjucks-parameterized project template that produces a startable project satisfying every Layer 1 structural conformance check, with pre-wired mandatory control stubs and pre-populated AI context, from a single scaffold runner invocation (`node scaffold.js`). The template directory lives at `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` (for example, `catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/` and `catalog/templates/gp-001-java/` for a path with two approved stacks). It is versioned alongside the Golden Path specification and Verification Contract.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/                   ← Template root
├── template.yaml                                   ← Backstage Software Template manifest (spec.parameters + spec.steps)
├── scaffold-validation.yaml                        ← Subset of Verification Contract (Layer 1 checks)
└── skeleton/                                       ← Source files rendered by fetch:template / node scaffold.js
    └── __service_name__/                           ← Instantiated project root (filename token substituted at run time)
    ├── src/
    │   ├── api/                                    ← SC-001: API handler layer
    │   │   ├── HealthController.java               ← Health endpoint stub (SC-003)
    │   │   └── package-info.java
    │   ├── domain/                                 ← SC-001: Business logic layer
    │   │   └── package-info.java
    │   └── infrastructure/                         ← SC-001: External integrations layer
    │       ├── AuditEventPublisher.java            ← Mandatory control stub
    │       └── package-info.java
    ├── docs/
    │   └── openapi.yaml                            ← SC-002 + SC-003: OpenAPI 3.1 spec w/ /health defined
    ├── .ai/
    │   ├── context.yaml                            ← Pre-populated: Golden Path ID, compliance scope
    │   ├── constraints.md                          ← Pre-populated: Path-specific prohibitions and mandates
    │   ├── instructions.md                         ← Pre-populated: Tool-agnostic agent instructions
    │   └── catalog-ref.yaml                        ← Pre-populated: Catalog API endpoint reference
    ├── k8s/
    │   ├── deployment.yaml                         ← ESO SecretStore reference pre-wired
    │   └── externalsecret.yaml                     ← ESO ExternalSecret stub for path-standard secrets
    ├── src/main/resources/
    │   ├── application.yaml                        ← Structured logging, trace ID injection pre-configured
    │   └── logback-spring.xml                      ← PiiRedactionSerializer registered
    ├── service.yaml                                ← Service declaration: team, domain, golden_path_id
    ├── pom.xml                                     ← Approved dependencies from registry.gainwell.internal
    └── SET_AI_CONTEXT.md                           ← Human-readable AI context summary
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|
| `template.yaml` | Backstage Software Template manifest. Declares the required parameters (`service_name`, `team`, `domain`), optional parameters with defaults (e.g., `dotnet_version`), and path constants (e.g., `golden_path_id`, `compliance_scope`). The `spec.steps` block documents the scaffolding pipeline; `node scaffold.js` executes the fetch step locally until a developer portal platform is adopted. | None |
| `scaffold-validation.yaml` | Layer 1 check subset from the path's Verification Contract. Run by `conformance-check --validate-scaffold` to verify the template itself before publication. | PTN-GOV-AI-003 |
| `src/api/` | Layer for API handlers, controllers, routes, and request/response types. Pre-created with a `HealthController` stub and `package-info.java`. | SC-001 |
| `src/domain/` | Layer for business logic, services, and domain model types. Pre-created empty with `package-info.java` establishing the package namespace. | SC-001 |
| `src/infrastructure/` | Layer for external integrations: repository implementations, Kafka producers, external service clients. Pre-created with `AuditEventPublisher` stub. | SC-001 |
| `docs/openapi.yaml` | OpenAPI 3.1 specification template. Pre-defines `GET /health` returning `200 { "status": "UP", "version": "<semver>" }` and `GET /info`. Teams extend this file for their API endpoints. | SC-002, SC-003 |
| `k8s/externalsecret.yaml` | External Secrets Operator `ExternalSecret` manifest stub referencing the path-standard Key Vault path naming convention. Teams add secret keys; they do not change the store reference. | PTN-APP-GOV-002 (ESO constraint) |
| `src/main/resources/logback-spring.xml` | Logback configuration with `PiiRedactionSerializer` registered for all JSON appenders. PHI field redaction is active from the first log output. | PTN-APP-GOV-002 (PHI constraint) |
| `src/infrastructure/AuditEventPublisher.java` | Pre-wired Kafka producer stub publishing to the `audit-events` topic. Teams call `publish(event)` from domain operations; they do not configure the topic or producer. | PTN-APP-GOV-002 (audit constraint) |
| `.ai/context.yaml` | Pre-populated with the Golden Path ID, compliance scope (HIPAA, FedRAMP as applicable), and parameterized service name and team. | PTN-APP-GOV-002 |
| `.ai/constraints.md` | Pre-populated with the path's mandatory controls and prohibited patterns, drawn from the path's `constraints.md` source in the catalog. | PTN-APP-GOV-002 |
| `service.yaml` | Backstage Component entity descriptor. Pre-populated with parameterized `metadata.name` (`service_name`), `spec.owner` (`team`), `spec.system` (`domain`), and Golden Path annotations as path constants. | PTN-GOV-AI-001 |
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

1. Platform Engineering authors the scaffold template from the mandatory structure defined by this pattern, guided by the GUID-APP-IMPL-003 scaffold authoring methodology
2. Platform Engineering runs `conformance-check --validate-scaffold catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` against `scaffold-validation.yaml` to verify the template itself passes all Layer 1 checks before submission
3. ARB reviews and approves the scaffold template as part of the complete Golden Path bundle (Terraform module, application scaffold, CI/CD pipeline template, security template, compliance metadata)
4. Development team or autonomous pipeline runs `node scaffold.js` against `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` with `service_name`, `team`, `domain` inputs; receives a populated project directory
5. Team opens the repository: `.ai/context.yaml` and `.ai/constraints.md` are present; AI agents load correct context on first invocation
6. Team makes their first commit. CI/CD pipeline runs the Conformance Gate (PTN-INFRA-GOV-001). All Layer 1 structural checks pass against the unmodified scaffold output.
7. Team adds business logic to `src/domain/` and API handlers to `src/api/`. They call `auditEventPublisher.publish(event)` in domain operations; they extend `docs/openapi.yaml` for their specific API paths.
page_texts.19:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

**Multi-language paths**: A Golden Path with more than one approved stack (for example, GP-001 approves Java 21/Spring Boot and Python 3.12/FastAPI) requires one scaffold template per approved stack variant. Each variant is stored at a language-qualified path: `catalog/templates/gp-001-java/` and `catalog/templates/gp-001-python/`. Both must satisfy the same Verification Contract structural checks; language-specific file paths differ but the logical structure remains consistent.

**Batch/Worker paths**: Golden Paths without HTTP API surfaces (scheduled batch jobs, queue workers) omit `docs/openapi.yaml` and the `src/api/` layer. Their Verification Contracts will not contain SC-002 or SC-003. The mandatory control stubs for audit event publishing and secret management remain present.

**React Micro-Frontend paths**: Front-end Golden Paths have an entirely different directory structure (no Java layer separation). Their scaffolds must still include `.ai/`, `service.yaml`, `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md`, and any applicable compliance metadata annotations; structural conformance checks are defined per-path in the Verification Contract.

**Developer Portal Forward Compatibility**: The template structure conventions used by this pattern are deliberately aligned with the [Backstage.io](https://backstage.io) Software Templates model so that templates can be adopted by a developer portal platform without changes to any template file content. The specific choices and their future-compatibility rationale are:

| Convention | Choice | Why | What changes at adoption ||
|---|---|---|---|
| Template manifest format | `apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3 / kind: Template` with `spec.parameters` (JSON Schema) and `spec.steps` | This is the native Backstage Software Template manifest format. `node scaffold.js` reads the same file today. | Delete `scaffold.js`; point Backstage at the catalog directory. |
| Template file expression delimiter | `${{ values.variable }}` | Backstage's `fetch:template` action uses this non-standard Nunjucks prefix specifically to avoid conflicts with other template types. Using it now means template files are already in the correct syntax. | None — files are already correct. |
| Template source directory | `skeleton/` | Backstage's `fetch:template` default source path is `skeleton/` (via `url: ./skeleton`). Using it now means no path change is needed. | None — `url: ./skeleton` is already in `spec.steps`. |
| Filename tokens | `__variable__` | Native Backstage `fetch:template` filename token convention. | None — already correct. |
| Service catalog entity | `apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1 / kind: Component` | Native Backstage catalog entity format. When Backstage is adopted, the `catalog:register` step (already commented in `spec.steps`) reads `service.yaml` directly. | Uncomment `publish` and `catalog:register` steps in `spec.steps`. |

Adopting a developer portal platform therefore requires: (1) deploying a Backstage instance, (2) pointing it at the catalog directory, (3) uncommenting the `publish` and `catalog:register` steps in each `template.yaml`. No template file content changes are needed.
page_texts.21:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- The Golden Path's Verification Contract is drafted and its Layer 1 structural checks are finalized (PTN-GOV-AI-003). The scaffold cannot be validated until the checks it must satisfy are defined.
- The Golden Path's `constraints.md` is authored (PTN-APP-GOV-002). The scaffold pre-populates `.ai/constraints.md` from this file; the source must exist.
- At least one approved language/framework stack is identified for the path. The scaffold is language-specific; this decision must be made before authoring begins.
- Platform Engineering has Node.js available to run `node scaffold.js` and `conformance-check` to validate the template.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-1-template-root-and-parameterization]

#### Phase 1: Template Root and Parameterization

1. Create `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/template.yaml` as a Backstage Software Template manifest declaring the three required inputs and path-specific optional parameters:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
   kind: Template
   metadata:
     name: {path-id}-{language}
   spec:
     parameters:
       - title: Service Details
         required:
           - service_name
           - team
           - domain
         properties:
           service_name:
             title: Service Name
             type: string
             description: "Lowercase kebab-case name for the service (e.g. claims-eligibility-api)"
             pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
           team:
             title: Owning Team
             type: string
             description: "Team identifier in the platform directory"
           domain:
             title: Business Domain
             type: string
             description: "Business domain this service belongs to (e.g. eligibility, claims)"
           dotnet_version:
             title: .NET Version
             type: string
             default: "8.0"
             enum: ["8.0"]
             description: "Approved .NET runtime version for this path"
     steps:
       - id: fetch
         name: Fetch Scaffold Template
         action: fetch:template
         input:
           url: ./skeleton
           values:
             service_name: ${{ parameters.service_name }}
             team: ${{ parameters.team }}
             domain: ${{ parameters.domain }}
             dotnet_version: ${{ parameters.dotnet_version }}
             golden_path: GP-001            # path constant
             compliance_scope: HIPAA        # path constant
             workload_class: hipaa-rest-microservice  # path constant
   ```
   No additional required parameters. Optional parameters must have valid defaults. Path constants (Golden Path ID, compliance scope, workload class) belong in `spec.steps[].input.values` — not exposed as team inputs. The `spec.steps` block fully describes the future Backstage pipeline; `node scaffold.js` executes the fetch step locally by reading this same file.

2. Create the `skeleton/` subdirectory in the template root. All project template files live under `skeleton/`. The scaffold runner renders `skeleton/` into the output directory; when a developer portal platform is adopted, `fetch:template` points to `url: ./skeleton` — which is the default — with no other change. Create the `__service_name__/` root directory inside `skeleton/`.
page_texts.24:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-2-directory-structure-sc-001]

#### Phase 2: Directory Structure (SC-001)

3. Create `src/api/`, `src/domain/`, `src/infrastructure/` directories under `src/`. Each directory must contain at least one file (the conformance check cannot detect empty directories in most VCS implementations). Use a `package-info.java` (Java), `__init__.py` (Python), or `doc.go` (Go) as the minimum presence file.

4. Create the `HealthController` stub in `src/api/`. This is the implementation of the health endpoint that Layer 2 fitness functions will invoke. It must:
   - Handle `GET /health`
   - Return HTTP 200 with body `{"status":"UP","version":"0.1.0"}` (or the language-equivalent; version is a path constant in the scaffold, not a template parameter)
   - Return HTTP 503 with body `{"status":"DOWN"}` if application-defined readiness conditions are not met

5. Create the `AuditEventPublisher` stub in `src/infrastructure/`. This is a concrete class (not an interface) that teams instantiate and call. It must compile without additional wiring. Pre-wire the Kafka topic name as a constant matching the path-standard value (`audit-events`). Pre-wire the producer configuration to read bootstrap servers from the External Secrets Operator-managed secret reference for this path.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-3-required-files]

#### Phase 3: Required Files

6. Create `docs/openapi.yaml` (SC-002). The template file must include:
   - `openapi: '3.1.0'`
   - `info.title`: `${{ values.service_name }}`
   - `paths./health.get`: defined, returning `200` with schema `{status: string, version: string}` (SC-003)
   - `paths./info.get`: defined, returning service metadata
   - `components.schemas.HealthResponse`: defines the health response schema
   Teams add their business API paths to this file. The mandatory system paths must not be removed.

7. Create `service.yaml` as a Backstage Component entity descriptor in the project root:
   ```yaml
   apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1
   kind: Component
   metadata:
     name: "${{ values.service_name }}"
     annotations:
       golden-path/id: "{path-id-constant}"           # path constant — do not parameterize
       golden-path/version: "{version-constant}"      # path constant — do not parameterize
       golden-path/compliance-scope: "{scope-constant}"  # path constant — do not parameterize
       golden-path/workload-class: "{class-constant}"    # path constant — do not parameterize
   spec:
     type: service
     lifecycle: experimental
     owner: "${{ values.team }}"
     system: "${{ values.domain }}"
   ```
   When a developer portal platform is adopted, `catalog:register` reads this file and creates the catalog entry automatically — no migration needed.
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-4-pre-wired-mandatory-controls]

#### Phase 4: Pre-Wired Mandatory Controls

8. Configure structured logging. For Java/Spring: create `src/main/resources/logback-spring.xml` with the `PiiRedactionSerializer` added to the JSON encoder. The class must be on the classpath (include the dependency in `pom.xml`). For Python/FastAPI: configure the `structlog` processor chain in `config/logging.py` with the PHI redaction filter registered.

9. Configure External Secrets Operator. Create `k8s/externalsecret.yaml` referencing the path-standard `SecretStore` and Key Vault path prefix. Teams add their specific secret keys to the `spec.data` array; they do not change the store reference, refresh interval, or target secret name prefix. Create `k8s/deployment.yaml` with the standard container spec, resource limits matching path defaults, and `envFrom` referencing the ESO-managed secret.

10. Configure observability instrumentation in `application.yaml` (or language-equivalent): structured log format, trace ID injection from incoming request headers, Prometheus metrics endpoint at `/actuator/prometheus` (Spring) or `/metrics` (FastAPI/Prometheus client), log level configuration reading from environment variable with a safe default.
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-5-ai-context-pre-population]

#### Phase 5: AI Context Pre-Population

11. Create `.ai/context.yaml` pre-populated from the path's defined values (see PTN-APP-GOV-002 for the schema). Service name and team use `${{ values.service_name }}` and `${{ values.team }}` Nunjucks expressions. Compliance scope, `golden_path.id`, `golden_path.catalog_url`, and `stack` fields are path constants. Do not leave these as placeholders; teams should not need to edit this file after instantiation.

12. Create `.ai/constraints.md` by copying the path's `constraints.md` source from the catalog. This is a direct copy, not a reference, so the file is available in the repository without requiring a catalog fetch. It will be updated by the catalog version updater action when a new path version is published.

13. Create `.ai/catalog-ref.yaml` pre-populated with the catalog API endpoint, the path ID, and `auto_update: true`. The pinned version should match the current catalog version at scaffold template publication time; it will be updated by the catalog version updater action thereafter.

14. Create `.ai/instructions.md` as the tool-agnostic agent instruction file. Summarize the active Golden Path ID, the three most critical constraints, and the catalog URL in plain prose. This single file serves all AI coding tools — GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Google Code Assist, and autonomous pipeline agents — without duplication.

15. Create `SET_AI_CONTEXT.md` in the project root as the human-readable context summary, linking to the `.ai/` files and providing the path's catalog URL.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#phase-6-scaffold-validation-and-arb-submission]

#### Phase 6: Scaffold Validation and ARB Submission

16. Create `scaffold-validation.yaml` in the template root. This file is a copy of the Layer 1 checks from the path's Verification Contract (all checks with `layer: 1`). It is used by `conformance-check --validate-scaffold` to verify the template produces conformant output.

17. Run a test instantiation via `node scaffold.js --config catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/template.yaml --service-name test-svc --team test-team --domain test-domain`.

18. Run `conformance-check --path-id {path-id} --validate-scaffold` against the instantiated output. All Layer 1 checks must pass. If any fail, correct the template and re-validate.

19. Confirm the instantiated project compiles and the health endpoint starts (`mvn spring-boot:run` or `uvicorn main:app` or equivalent). The health endpoint must return HTTP 200 from `GET /health` with no additional configuration.

20. Include the scaffold template in the ARB submission package alongside the Terraform module, CI/CD pipeline template, security template, and compliance metadata. The ARB checklist (PTN-GOV-AI-001) requires "All template components present" as a hard gate.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#example-1-templateyaml--backstage-software-template-manifest]

#### Example 1: `template.yaml` — Backstage Software Template Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: gp-001-dotnet
  title: GP-001 HIPAA REST Microservice (.NET 8)
  description: >
    Golden Path GP-001 — HIPAA-compliant REST microservice on AKS, .NET 8 / ASP.NET Core.
  tags: [golden-path, hipaa, dotnet]
spec:
  owner: platform-engineering
  type: service
  parameters:
    - title: Service Details
      required: [service_name, team, domain]
      properties:
        service_name:
          title: Service Name
          type: string
          description: Lowercase kebab-case name for the service (e.g. claims-eligibility-api)
          pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$'
        team:
          title: Owning Team
          type: string
          description: Team identifier in the platform directory
        domain:
          title: Business Domain
          type: string
          description: Domain this service belongs to (e.g. eligibility, claims, provider)
        dotnet_version:
          title: .NET Version
          type: string
          default: '8.0'
          enum: ['8.0']
          description: Approved .NET runtime version for this path
  steps:
    - id: fetch
      name: Fetch Scaffold Template
      action: fetch:template
      input:
        url: ./skeleton          # Project template files live here
        values:
          service_name: ${{ parameters.service_name }}
          team: ${{ parameters.team }}
          domain: ${{ parameters.domain }}
          dotnet_version: ${{ parameters.dotnet_version }}
          golden_path: GP-001
          compliance_scope: HIPAA
          workload_class: hipaa-rest-microservice
          keyvault_name: gainwell-hipaa-kv
          audit_event_bus: audit-events
    # When a developer portal platform is adopted, add:
    # - id: publish
    #   action: publish:github
    #   ...
    # - id: register
    #   action: catalog:register
    #   input:
    #     catalogInfoPath: /service.yaml
```

The scaffold runner (`node scaffold.js`) reads this file, extracts defaults from `spec.parameters[].properties` and constants from `spec.steps[].input.values`, then renders the `skeleton/` directory with Nunjucks using `${{ values.variable }}` expressions.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#example-4-scaffold-validationyaml]

#### Example 4: `scaffold-validation.yaml`

```yaml
# scaffold-validation.yaml
# Layer 1 checks from VC-GP-001 used by `conformance-check --validate-scaffold`
# This file travels with the scaffold template — update it when the Verification Contract changes.
scaffold_validation:
  path_id: GP-001
  checks:
    - id: SC-001
      description: "src/ with api/, domain/, infrastructure/ subdirectories present"
      type: directory_presence
      paths:
        - src/api
        - src/domain
        - src/infrastructure
    - id: SC-002
      description: "docs/openapi.yaml present"
      type: file_presence
      path: docs/openapi.yaml
    - id: SC-003
      description: "GET /health defined in OpenAPI spec"
      type: openapi_path_presence
      spec: docs/openapi.yaml
      method: get
      path: /health
    - id: SC-004
      description: "service.yaml present as Backstage Component entity with golden-path/id annotation"
      type: yaml_field_presence
      file: service.yaml
      field: metadata.annotations["golden-path/id"]
    - id: SC-005
      description: ".ai/context.yaml present"
      type: file_presence
      path: .ai/context.yaml
    - id: SC-006
      description: ".ai/constraints.md present"
      type: file_presence
      path: .ai/constraints.md
```

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- **Maintain the four forward-compatibility conventions without deviation.** The `${{ values.` expression delimiter, `skeleton/` source directory, Backstage `spec.parameters` manifest format, and `backstage.io/v1alpha1 kind: Component` entity format are not arbitrary choices — they are the exact conventions used by Backstage's Software Templates. Changing any of them (for example, reverting to `{{ variable }}` or renaming `skeleton/` to `template/`) eliminates the zero-rework path to developer portal adoption and forces a mass find-and-replace across every template file in the catalog at adoption time.
- **Author the Verification Contract checks first, the scaffold second.** The scaffold's job is to pass those checks. Authoring them in order ensures the scaffold is purpose-built to satisfy the checks rather than checks being backfilled to describe what the scaffold happens to produce.
- **All stubs must compile and the project must start before submission.** "Stubs" does not mean placeholder code. `AuditEventPublisher` must produce a valid Kafka `ProducerRecord`. The health controller must return HTTP 200. Compile errors or runtime startup failures in the unmodified scaffold output are blocking defects.
- **Narrow the parameterization scope deliberately.** The three required parameters (`service_name`, `team`, `domain`) are intentionally minimal. Every additional required parameter is a decision the team must make during instantiation that could produce variation. Compliance-sensitive defaults belong in the template manifest as path constants, not as team-provided values.
- **Treat `.ai/constraints.md` as a living file managed by the catalog version updater.** Platform Engineering does not instruct teams to keep constraints files current — the catalog version updater action opens a pull request against each repository when a path version is published. Do not embed logic in the constraint file that teams must interpret; keep it machine-processable as well as human-readable.
- **Include a `GETTING_STARTED.md` in the scaffold.** After instantiation, teams should know exactly what they have, what they should NOT change (mandatory control stubs, `.ai/` files, `service.yaml` constants), and what they are expected to add (domain model, API business logic, PHI field names in `context.yaml`).

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Deviating from the forward-compatibility conventions in new templates.** Using `{{ variable }}` instead of `${{ values.variable }}`, or `template/` instead of `skeleton/`, or a custom manifest schema instead of `apiVersion: scaffolder.backstage.io/v1beta3`, creates a two-tier catalog where some templates are developer portal-ready and others require conversion. When a developer portal platform is eventually adopted, the non-conforming templates are blocked until individually migrated. Consistency across the catalog is the invariant to protect.
- **Omitting the `scaffold-validation.yaml` and skipping pre-submission validation.** The scaffold reaches teams with a structural defect that is immediately caught on the first pipeline run. Every team using the path is affected until the template is corrected and teams re-instantiate or manually patch.
- **Providing control stubs as interface definitions rather than concrete implementations.** Teams choose their own implementation, reproduce the Kafka configuration or PHI redaction logic incorrectly, and surface the compliance violations at Layer 2 fitness function checks or in audit review. Concrete stubs with correct configuration eliminate this variation.
- **Using placeholder text in `.ai/context.yaml` compliance scope or PHI fields.** The AI agent reads these values at generation time. A placeholder value (for example, `compliance_scope: [TODO]`) causes the agent to reason without compliance context and generates output that does not apply PHI handling rules.
- **Publishing a scaffold template before the Verification Contract is finalized.** If the contract is updated with additional structural checks after publication, every team that instantiated the scaffold must manually add the missing structure. Contract-first ordering prevents this.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

The scaffold template participates in HIPAA and FedRAMP compliance by construction:

- **PHI handling**: `PiiRedactionSerializer` registered in structured logging configuration from the first commit prevents PHI from appearing in log output, which would constitute a potential unauthorized disclosure.
- **Secret management**: ESO `ExternalSecret` configuration eliminates the ability to mount secrets as environment variables (a PHI/FedRAMP prohibited pattern) from the project baseline.
- **Audit trail**: `AuditEventPublisher` stub enables teams to satisfy audit event requirements for PHI data access operations without configuring the Kafka producer independently.
page_texts.39:
[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

The scaffold template is not published independently. It is submitted as the application scaffold component of the complete Golden Path bundle. The ARB checklist (PTN-GOV-AI-001) includes "All template components present (Terraform, scaffold, CI/CD, security, compliance metadata)" as a hard gate that blocks publication until satisfied.

A scaffold template update that changes the directory structure, removes or modifies pre-wired controls, or introduces new parameterization inputs requires a new Golden Path version and ARB review. Updates limited to dependency version bumps or documentation corrections may follow the minor update process defined in PTN-GOV-AI-001.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#real-world-example-1-gp-001-hipaa-rest-microservice-initial-scaffold]

### Real-World Example 1: GP-001 HIPAA REST Microservice Initial Scaffold

**Context:** GP-001 is the first Golden Path published for Gainwell's HIPAA-compliant REST microservice workload class. It is the highest-priority path in the initial catalog build.

**Implementation:** Platform Engineering authored the Verification Contract first, establishing SC-001 through SC-006 as the Layer 1 checks. The scaffold template was built to produce a project passing all six checks from the cookiecutter instantiation. The `AuditEventPublisher` stub was implemented as a concrete Spring `@Component` bean with the Kafka producer pre-configured to write to `audit-events`. The `PiiRedactionSerializer` was added to `logback-spring.xml` with the PHI field filter initialized from a configuration property (so teams populate `phi_fields` in `context.yaml` without modifying the logging configuration). On the first ARB submission, one issue was found during scaffold validation: the Java-generated `package-info.java` files did not survive Git's empty-directory behavior. The fix was to add a `.gitkeep` comment file in addition to `package-info.java`. The scaffold passed all validation checks after the fix.

**Outcome:** Seven product teams instantiated GP-001 in the first 30 days of catalog publication. All seven passed their first pipeline run without structural remediation.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#real-world-example-2-scaffold-defect-discovery-and-remediation]

### Real-World Example 2: Scaffold Defect Discovery and Remediation

**Context:** GP-003 (Event-Driven Consumer Service, Java/Spring) was published with a scaffold template authored before this pattern was established. The scaffold was missing `docs/openapi.yaml` because the original author believed event-driven services do not have HTTP APIs.

**Implementation:** The Verification Contract for GP-003 included SC-002 and SC-003 because the Golden Path requires all services to expose `/health` regardless of whether they have a business API. Teams instantiating GP-003 encountered SC-002 and SC-003 failures on their first pipeline run and were confused about why an event-driven service needed an OpenAPI spec. Platform Engineering created a corrected scaffold template (v1.1.0) with `docs/openapi.yaml` containing only the system paths (`/health`, `/info`). A migration script updated existing GP-003 repositories to add the missing file.

**Lesson Learned:** The Layer 1 check set (and therefore the Verification Contract) should be finalized before the scaffold is authored. Scaffold defects discovered post-publication require migration scripts and coordination across all consuming teams.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#scenario-1-autonomous-ai-pipeline-service-instantiation]

#### Scenario 1: Autonomous AI Pipeline Service Instantiation

**Scenario Description:** An intent-to-infrastructure pipeline (PTN-TEC-AI-001) receives a structured intent document for a new HIPAA-scoped eligibility API and selects GP-001 as the applicable Golden Path.

**Guidance Application:** The pipeline runs `node scaffold.js` against `catalog/templates/gp-001-dotnet/` with `service_name`, `team`, and `domain` values extracted from the intent document. The AI agent then generates the domain model and API handlers, extending the scaffold's `src/domain/` and `src/api/` layers. Because `.ai/context.yaml` is pre-populated with the correct compliance scope and PHI field constraints, the agent applies PHI redaction to any fields declared in the intent document's data classification section. The scaffold's pre-wired `AuditEventPublisher` is referenced in the generated domain service; no additional Kafka configuration is needed.

#### Scenario 2: Development Team Blue-Green Path Migration

**Scenario Description:** A team running on a deprecated version of GP-001 needs to migrate to GP-001 v2.0, which introduced a new required directory (added to SC-001) and a new mandatory compliance annotation in `service.yaml`.

**Guidance Application:** Platform Engineering publishes a migration guide alongside the v2.0 scaffold. The guide specifies exactly which files changed between scaffold versions. The catalog version updater action opens a pull request against each GP-001 repository with the `.ai/constraints.md` update. For structural changes (new directory, updated `service.yaml`), the migration PR also includes the structural additions. Teams review and merge; conformance gates validate the merged state.

[patterns/application/governance/PTN-APP-GOV-004-golden-path-scaffold-template-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** No specification exists for what a Golden Path scaffold template must contain, resulting in scaffolds that produce services failing Layer 1 conformance checks, missing mandatory runtime control stubs, and offering no pre-populated AI context.

**Solution:** A Golden Path scaffold template stored at `catalog/templates/{path-id}-{language}/` must produce, from a single `node scaffold.js` invocation, a compilable project that passes all Layer 1 structural checks, includes concrete stubs for all mandatory runtime controls, and contains pre-populated `.ai/` context files. The template manifest (`template.yaml`) declares the required inputs and defaults. The scaffold is run with Node.js to instantiate the project, and is validated by running Layer 1 checks against its own output before ARB submission.

**When to Use:**
- Authoring any new Golden Path scaffold template
- Auditing or remediating an existing scaffold for structural or compliance gaps
- Extending a scaffold when a path version update introduces new structural rules

**Key Benefits:**
- Services pass Layer 1 on first pipeline run with no structural remediation
- Mandatory controls (PHI redaction, ESO, audit events) are pre-wired from the starting commit
- AI agents have correct context from the first invocation in a newly instantiated repository

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium — requires knowledge of the target language/framework, the path's Verification Contract checks, the mandatory controls defined in `constraints.md`, and Nunjucks template authoring

**Prerequisites:** Verification Contract (Layer 1 checks finalized), `constraints.md` authored, approved language stack identified

**Related Patterns:** PTN-GOV-AI-001, PTN-GOV-AI-003, PTN-APP-GOV-001, PTN-APP-GOV-002, PTN-INFRA-GOV-001, PTN-INFRA-GOV-003
